page: Google Cloud Platform c4-highmem-32 is a memory-dense compute instance based on the x86_64 architecture. It is powered by a dedicated Intel Xeon 8581C processor operating at 2.3 GHz, delivering 32 vCPUs across 16 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading enabled. The system features a substantial 260 MB L3 cache alongside 248 GB of system memory, providing 7.75 GB of RAM per vCPU. The underlying processor includes hardware support for advanced vector and matrix math extensions such as AVX-512 and Intel AMX, alongside cryptographic accelerations including AES, VAES, and SHA-NI. The instance does not include integrated local storage or dedicated hardware GPUs, relying instead on network-attached storage and standard network configurations without complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark results show robust performance in specific memory-bound and vectorized workloads. The instance achieves a top-tier result in small model (135M) LLM text generation at 421.19 tokens per second and strong prompt processing throughput of 2850.19 tokens per second, aided by AMX matrix instructions. It also exhibits strong throughput in static web serving at 51.15 GB per second, as well as strong Geekbench image and text processing scores. General compute metrics, including Geekbench single-core (1933.0) and multi-core (15636.0), alongside PassMark CPU scores, fall in the mid-range spectrum. Memory write bandwidth reaches 61.79 GB per second, while read bandwidth on large blocks reaches 144.63 GB per second. The primary constraint is observed in heavy computational tasks lacking GPU acceleration, such as large 70B parameter model text generation, which drops to 2.38 tokens per second.

With its generous 7.75 GB of RAM per vCPU, c4-highmem-32 provides qualitative cost efficiency for memory-intensive applications that do not require dedicated hardware accelerators. The large memory pool and 260 MB shared L3 cache make the configuration suitable for in-memory databases, large Redis deployments (benchmarked at 39.05 million SET operations per second), intermediate data transformations, enterprise caching layers, and lightweight CPU-based inference pipelines.
description: Google Cloud Platform c4-highmem-32 is a high-memory compute instance powered by an Intel Xeon 8581C processor clocked at 2.3 GHz. Configured with 32 vCPUs across 16 physical cores and 248 GB of system memory, the instance delivers a high memory-to-core ratio of 7.75 GB per vCPU alongside a 260 MB L3 cache. It integrates modern instruction sets including Intel AMX and AVX-512, which drive strong performance in lightweight LLM inference and static web serving reaching 51.15 GB per second. The server does not bundle local disk storage or hardware accelerators, leaving unaccelerated tasks such as large 70B parameter model text generation constrained. With dedicated x86_64 compute cores and substantial memory capacity, c4-highmem-32 is well aligned with memory-intensive workloads, including in-memory databases, caching tiers, ETL pipelines, and lightweight model serving.
